<!-- Generated by `bun run docs:api` from shared/src/api. Do not edit by hand. -->

The team server has 564 HTTP endpoints. Each one is declared once in [`shared/src/api/`](../../../shared/src/api/index.ts), with zod schemas for its query, body and response. The server validates every request against it, and the web app calls endpoints by name.

:::note
The API serves the Trina AX apps. It is not yet a stable public API for other programs, and it follows the [version rules](../develop/versioning.md).
:::

## Calling the API

- Endpoints live under the team's own address, for example `https://team.example.com/api/health`.
- The web app signs in with a session cookie. Requests from other origins are refused unless the origin is in `MYCEL_PUBLIC_ORIGINS`.
- Live updates and answers stream over a WebSocket at `GET /api/ws`.
- The [MCP connector](../agents/mcp-connector.md) adds `/mcp`, `/oauth/*` and `/.well-known/*` outside this list.

| Who | Means |
|---|---|
| Anyone | No session needed |
| Signed in | Any active member |
| Admin | An admin or the owner |
| Owner | The owner only |
| Owner + password | The owner, who enters their password again (updates, restores) |
| Admin + password | An admin or the owner, who enters their own password again (the team's AI connections) |

## Setup, sign-in and account

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/setup` | Anyone | Is first-run setup still needed (no owner yet)? |
| `POST` | `/api/setup` | Anyone | Create the team and its owner (only while no user exists; needs the setup token). Signs the owner in. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | Anyone | Sign in with username + password (argon2id). Rate-limited per IP and per account. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Signed in | End this session and clear the cookie. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/password` | Signed in | Change own password; ends every other session of this person. |
| `GET` | `/api/me` | Signed in | The signed-in person, groups, team name. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/me` | Signed in | Profile, language, theme and composer preferences. |
| `PUT` | `/api/me/web-access` | Signed in | Turn my "Allow all websites" for the AI's web reads on (with the current risk sentence accepted, while the team allows it) or off. |
| `GET` | `/api/me/usage` | Signed in | My own usage this day / week / month (never anyone else's) and the usage limits that apply to me. |
| `GET` | `/api/me/sessions` | Signed in | Own signed-in devices. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/me/sessions/:id` | Signed in | Sign out one of own devices. |
| `GET` | `/api/invites/:token` | Anyone | What an invite link is for (team name, role, still valid?). |
| `GET` | `/api/password-resets/:token` | Anyone | What a password reset link is for (whose account, still valid?). |
| `POST` | `/api/password-resets/:token` | Anyone | Set a new password with a one-time reset link; ends every other session and signs in. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/app-signin` | Signed in | Make a one-time code (3 minutes) that signs the desktop app in as me. Cookie sessions only; rate-limited; my earlier codes stop working. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/app-signin/redeem` | Anyone | Sign in with a one-time code from appSignIn (once, within 3 minutes). Sets the session cookie. |
| `POST` | `/api/invites/:token/accept` | Anyone | Create the account from an invite link and sign in. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/google/start` | Anyone | Start signing in with a connected Google account: Google's address to open. Rate-limited per IP. |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/google/redeem` | Anyone | Sign the desktop or phone app in with the one-time code from a Google sign-in (once, within 5 minutes, only with the app's secret). Sets the session cookie. |
| `POST` | `/api/setup/google` | Anyone | Start making the team and its owner with Google (only while no user exists; needs the setup token): Google's address to open. |
| `POST` | `/api/invites/google` | Anyone | Start joining with an invite and a Google account instead of a password (not for guest invites): Google's address to open. |
| `GET` | `/api/me/google` | Signed in | My connected Google account, and whether one can be connected here. |
| `POST` | `/api/me/google/connect` | Signed in | Start connecting my Google account (needs my current password, or a Google check without one): Google's address to open. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/me/google` | Signed in | Disconnect my Google account: it no longer signs me in. Refused (409) while I have no password. |
| `POST` | `/api/me/google/reauth` | Signed in | Start a Google check instead of the password (an account without one): Google's address to open in a new window, and the check's id. Refused while my re-check limit is locked. |
| `GET` | `/api/me/google/reauth/:id` | Signed in | Whether my Google check came back confirmed (only the session that started it; no-store). |
| `POST` | `/api/me/password` | Signed in | Set a first password for an account made with Google, after a Google check. Refused (409) when the account has a password. Other sessions stay; open reset links stop. |

## Chats and projects

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/questions/often-asked` | Signed in | Home’s "what my group often asks": generic sentences that 3 or more people of the caller’s group (else the team) asked in a similar way, rewritten once a day; never who asked, how many or when. Empty while the team setting is off or there is too little data. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats` | Signed in | Own chats and the shared project chats I wrote in, newest first (search with q, trash with trash=1: my own and the shared chats I deleted, while I may restore them). With projectId: my chats there and every shared chat of that project I can see. Every list but the trash gives each shared chat the other people who wrote in it (shared.people: the 3 most recent, never me; shared.peopleCount). Without q and trash, the first page starts with my pinned chats of that list (pinnedAt, the most recently pinned first) and the pages after it leave them out. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/groups` | Signed in | My Trina list in one read: my pinned chats, my chat folders, the projects I can see with my activity in the last 14 days (at most 8, the most recent first; projectsMore counts the rest I can see), each folder and project with how many of its chats I can open now, its first 3 and the ones that show a marker now, and page 1 of my other chats (next pages: GET /api/chats?other=1); each shared chat with the other people who wrote in it (shared.people, shared.peopleCount); projectActivity: for every project I can see, how many chats in it I can open (mine and its shared chats, never another person's private chat) and when the latest was active. Only what my own chat list holds and only projects I can see now; nobody else's folders. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats` | Signed in | New empty chat (optionally inside a project). In a team project it is a shared chat, seen and continued by the project's members, unless `private` is true ("Only me"); never in a personal project or while safe operations are on. |
| `GET` | `/api/engines` | Signed in | Whether the caller may pick the engine / model, the team default, and the engines + models they may pick. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id` | Signed in | One own chat, or a shared project chat I can see. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/queue` | Signed in | Own chat queue snapshot; advisory rank and epoch/revision for reconnect recovery. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/chats/:id` | Signed in | Rename, move to a project, change engine/model, or give a chat I continued from another a row of its own in my history ("Move out on its own", forkParent: null; its place in the list only, not its last activity; audited chat.fork_detach). A shared chat: its creator only, and it never changes project (409 shared_chat_move). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/chats/:id` | Signed in | Move to chat trash (purged after the team's chat retention). Stops a running turn. A shared chat: its creator or an editor of its project (audited when someone else); it is in its creator's trash and in the deleter's. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/restore` | Signed in | Bring a chat back from the trash. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/pin` | Signed in | Pin a chat I can see to the top of my chat list ("Pin to top"), for me only (a shared project chat too). Pinned already: unchanged. At most 50 pins (409 chat_pins_full). My other windows hear it (chat.updated). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/chats/:id/pin` | Signed in | Unpin a chat ("Unpin"); not pinned: unchanged. My other windows hear it (chat.updated). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/seen` | Signed in | I have this own chat on screen: its finished answers are seen (Chat.unseen goes away in every window and device). |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/messages` | Signed in | Active branch of the conversation, paged backwards. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages` | Signed in | Save the message, create the empty answer, queue the turn. Send the X-Mycel-Window header so browser tools reach this window. |
| `PUT` | `/api/chats/:id/waiting` | Signed in | A shared chat I may continue: how many of my messages wait there for the running answer to end (0: none). The server keeps it in memory for 45 s after the last call; a send there while someone else has waited longer is refused (409 shared_chat_next, naming nobody); a first place whose holder does not send within 12 s of holding someone back goes to the back of the line. The others see only how many other people wait (Chat.shared.waiting), told when someone starts or stops waiting. At most 30 a minute per person and chat (429). A chat of one person: nothing kept. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/stop` | Signed in | Stop the running or queued turn of this chat (a shared chat: only the person whose turn it is). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/share-to-room` | Signed in | Post a finished answer of my own AI chat to a room I am in, as my message (my note, then the answer as a quote), or as a reply in a message's thread there (threadRootId: a room's side chat). When some member cannot open a file it links to, or it carries content from material some cannot see, it first answers "confirm": a row per linked file and one provenance line, as counts and places I may look myself (never who), with a confirmKey; sent again with that key it posts, attaching the linked files asked for (attach). Older clients: confirm = the number of people. Rate-limited and notified like any message; audited. The AI's post_to_room tool (the person's own chat, after their yes on one server card) goes through the same checks and is audited with via ai. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/fork` | Signed in | Continue a chat in a new chat only I see, named "<title> (continued)": my own chat ("Continue in a new chat": everything on the branch, in its project while I see it) or a shared one ("Continue in a new chat only you see": in its project, a chat shared with people outside projects, as I see it now: other people's names kept, an answer hidden from me one line, a chat file by reference while I may still open it there). Its finished messages up to the end of the branch; the AI goes on from my own session of it (Claude Code) or from the copied history. The new chat sits under the chat in my history (Chat.forkParents). The original is not changed and nobody is told. Later edits there do not follow. Another person's chat that is not shared: 404. 409 with reason safe_ops, fork_not_here (a side chat or a scheduled run) or fork_nothing (no finished answer yet); 403 fork_guest (a guest outside their project or without AI). Audited (chat.fork). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/share` | Signed in | Share my private chat with its project's members (a team project that shares its chats). First a check of every branch: when its answers carry content from material some of them cannot see, or may have used my personal memories (or with ask), it answers "confirm" (how many, the places I may look myself, never who) with a confirmKey; sent again with that key it shares. Never undone. 409 with reason project_not_sharing, project_personal, project_in_trash, safe_ops, already_shared, scheduled_run, chat_busy or share_hidden. Rate-limited like a room message; audited. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/audience` | Signed in | Who a chat I can see is shared with: for a chat outside projects shared with people and groups, the people and groups by name (a group's size and the count only for its creator and admins when a group is in it); a shared project chat or my private chat lists nobody. Anyone who cannot see the chat gets the 404 of a missing chat. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/audience/preview` | Signed in | Dry run of a save of who sees a chat outside projects (its creator only, the same refusals as a save, chat_busy while a turn runs): what the people the list brings in would see that they could not before (counts of answers and places I may look myself, never who), and the key a save must carry. Nothing is saved. At most 60 a minute per person (429); the same list and chat state answers from a 60-second cache. |
| `PUT` | `/api/chats/:id/audience` | Signed in | Its creator saves who sees a chat outside projects (the whole list, at most 100 people and groups; [] makes it theirs alone again). Adds that bring in new people first answer "confirm" when its answers carry content from places some of them cannot open, may have used my memories, used recorded places they cannot open, or (a first share) will show them my earlier computer uploads (counts and places I may look myself, never who), with a confirmKey; sent again with that key it saves. Removed people's turns there stop first. A first share copies my earlier computer uploads into the chat (each at most 50 MB, metadata of photos cut out); filesNotCopied says how many could not be. 403 chat_share_creator_only to others who see it, the 404 of a missing chat to everyone else; 409 share_people_in_project, project_personal, safe_ops (adds), scheduled_run, side_chat, chat_busy (adds); 400 audience_full, unknown_subject (newly added only), needs_people. Rate-limited like a room message; audited (counts only); people added by name and through a group get an Inbox notice (at most one per chat and person a day). |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/users/:id/shared-chats` | Admin | For the delete-account dialog: how many chats this person shared with people and groups someone else sees now. Deleting the account deletes them for good after the retention period (disabling it keeps them). A count, nothing else. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/leave` | Signed in | "Leave this chat": someone a chat outside projects was shared with by name takes themselves out of it (docs/decisions/20261122-shared-chat-leave-and-lost-notices.md); their turns there stop and nothing of it stays theirs. Its creator gets 400 chat_leave_creator, a chat not shared with people 400 chat_leave_not_shared, someone who would still see it through a listed group 409 chat_leave_group; anyone who cannot see it the 404 of a missing chat. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/hide` | Signed in | "Hide from my list": a chat someone shared with me leaves my chat lists, for me only (search still finds it); opening it (POST /api/chats/:id/seen) or DELETE brings it back. Its creator gets 400 chat_hide_creator. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/mute` | Signed in | "Mute this chat": a chat shared with people, or a team project's shared chat, that I see stops telling me about new messages (no unread number, push or desktop notification); what was unread there is read. Mine only. 400 chat_mute_people_only for any other chat (a chat of one person); anyone who cannot see it gets the 404 of a missing chat. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/chats/:id/mute` | Signed in | Unmute a chat shared with people or a project's shared chat that I muted: its new messages tell me again. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/chats/:id/hide` | Signed in | Bring a chat I hid from my list back. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/files/:fileId` | Signed in | A file from the computer kept with a chat shared with people and groups (Attachment source chat), for whoever sees the chat now (checked on every read: anyone else, a removed person included, gets the 404 of a missing chat); one not sent in a message yet only for its sender. thumb=1 for an image preview, download=1 as an attachment, version=n an earlier version (the newest without it; one pruned or not of this chain: 404). Inline, a page or script type is sent as text/plain with a sandbox CSP: never a page of the app. A file on the safety check's download-only list is sent only with download=1 (503 quarantined otherwise). |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/files/:fileId/versions` | Signed in | The versions of a file kept with a chat shared with people (any id of its chain), oldest first: who saved each (or the AI for whom), when, its size; the newest marked head. canEdit: I may save a new version (a text file) now; canRestore: I may restore a version (any file) now. Anyone who may not open the file (the chat not theirs to see, an upload not sent yet, a file carried only by answers hidden from them) gets the 404 of a missing one: never a version, its name or how many. |
| `PUT` | `/api/chats/:id/files/:fileId/content` | Signed in | Save a text file of a chat shared with people as its new version (md, txt, csv, html, json; at most 10 MB): whoever may open the file and sees the chat. Nothing is overwritten: the chain keeps its last 20 versions. baseVersion: the version the editor read; someone saved since: beside true (both kept) and besideOf, the version saved in between. 409 chat_file_read_only for a project chat, a chat in the trash or a file that is not text; 409 safe_ops while safe operations are on; the 404 of a missing file for anyone who may not open it. Each person in the chat sees the change on its file tiles. At most 30 saves and restores a minute per person (429 with retryAfter). Audited (chat.file_version). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/files/:fileId/versions/:version/restore` | Signed in | Restore version :version of a file kept with a chat shared with people: a new newest version with its bytes; nothing is overwritten (at the 20-version cap the oldest after the first goes: pruned). The same rights, refusals and limit as a save. Audited (chat.file_restore). |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/thread` | Signed in | The thread under a finished AI answer of a shared chat I see: the answer as I see it and a page of the replies (newest page first, oldest first within it). People only: the AI never reads replies. A chat I do not see, a missing or hidden answer, a question or another chat's answer: the same 404. canReply false with readOnlyReason while safe operations are on, the chat is in the trash or no longer shared. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/thread` | Signed in | Reply under a finished answer (done or stopped) of a shared chat I may continue, as myself. The same clientId again returns the first reply. Access is checked before the sending budget (429 with retryAfter, the rooms' budget); at most 500 replies (409 thread_full). The answer's asker and everyone who replied get one Inbox notice per unread thread, and a push while "Replies in threads I'm part of" is on. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/chats/:id/thread-replies/:replyId` | Signed in | Delete a reply for everyone (no undo): its author, or whoever may moderate the chat (a project chat: its creator or a project editor; a chat shared with people: its creator). A moderator's delete is audited with ids only. A reply of another chat: 404. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/thread/read` | Signed in | I read a thread I follow up to this reply: its notice counts as read; my other windows hear it. Never past the thread's own replies. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/sources` | Signed in | The files the AI read or saw passages of for this answer, each checked against the viewer's access now (no name or path for the others). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/regenerate` | Signed in | New answer to the same user message (sibling of :messageId, an assistant message). |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/messages/:messageId/edit` | Signed in | Edited copy of user message :messageId as a new branch, then answer it. |
| `POST` | `/api/chats/:id/branch` | Signed in | Switch the visible branch ("< 2/3 >"); returns the newest page of the new path. |
| `GET` | `/api/chats/:id/requests` | Signed in | Open ask_user / browser site cards of the running turn of this chat. |
| `POST` | `/api/turns/:id/connect` | Signed in | Finish a connect_service card: add the connection with a sealed key, after a sign-in, or skip |
| `GET` | `/api/turns/:id/requests/:requestId/details/:index` | Signed in | The whole text of a card detail that the card carries only the start of (ConfirmDetail.fullChars), of an own open card. |
| `POST` | `/api/turns/:id/answer` | Signed in | Answer an ask_user card or a browser site confirmation of an own running turn. |
| `GET` | `/api/projects` | Signed in | Projects whose folder the caller can read; manage=1 (the owner and admins): also the team projects they manage without being a member, without their contents; and for everyone the team projects in the trash they are a member of (name and state only). |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/update-notice` | Signed in | For the owner or an admin: the team projects from before the update to members-only projects (0.4.0 to 0.5.0) that they read by their role then and do not read now, by name, for one card on Admin › Home. Empty for members, after the card was dismissed, and for people who were not the owner or an admin at the update. |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/update-notice/join` | Signed in | "Add me to these": the caller becomes a member of every project on their card, each saved as Add me on the project saves it (audited per project with self, its members told), plus one audit row. Projects not on the card are never touched; one that cannot be saved is skipped and counted. |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/update-notice/dismiss` | Signed in | Hide the card for good, for the caller (every device). |
| `POST` | `/api/projects` | Signed in | New project: a new team project folder projects/<name> with participants (members too, unless the team lets only admins), or a personal one in users/<me>/projects/<name>. Nowhere else. |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/access-preview` | Signed in | Dry run: how many people would see a new team project with these participants (for the owner and admins also apart: by its rules, by role only), or (projectId: its creator or an admin) who gains and loses an existing one, what the people who gain it would see, and whether saving also writes the floor rule or puts the creator's rule back (the screen asks first then). Nothing is saved. At most 60 a minute per person (429). |
| `POST` | `/api/sharing/widening-answers` | Signed in | The widening list: the answers of a team project's shared chats (target project) or of one chat outside projects (target chat: its Share dialog's whole list in add; its creator only) that the people its Members dialog would add start seeing although they used places some of them can't open, newest first, 20 a page (the caller's own view: answers hidden from them left out, a place by name only when they may open it, "missed by" only the people and groups they picked). Whoever may change its members (403 widening_not_allowed to another viewer, 404 to anyone else). The first page takes a room-send token (429); a cursor of a list whose people or position changed answers 409 changed. Nothing is saved. |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id` | Signed in | One project (manage=1: also one the owner or an admin manages without being a member, without its contents, or one in the trash the caller is a member of: name and state only). |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/restore` | Signed in | Put a team project whose folder is in the trash back, with its folder (the owner or an admin, or its creator while a member; audited). |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/people` | Signed in | Who is in a team project in projects/<name>, each person once with their photo, groups expanded (the groups only for whoever manages it). Its members, and the owner and admins who manage it; anyone else 404. 409 project_personal for a personal project, project_legacy for one made before outside projects/. |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/:id/access` | Signed in | Who sees a team project: its participants, the rules the project screen does not change, the rules hash (its creator or an admin). |
| `PUT` | `/api/projects/:id/participants` | Signed in | Change who sees a team project in projects/<name> (its creator or an admin): the folder rules, as Admin › Folder permissions saves them (409 rules_changed when they changed since expectedHash; audited; people who lose it lose its shared chats). |
| `PATCH` | `/api/projects/:id` | Signed in | Edit name / instructions (the creator or an admin, with write access to the folder; audited, readers notified). shareChats: false is 409 share_chats_always (a team project always shares its new chats). folderPath: admins only, for a project whose folder is in the trash or missing, to an existing projects/<name>. |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/share` | Signed in | Make a personal project a team project: a new projects/<name> with participants, the files copied into it, the project pointed at it; then the personal folder goes to the caller's trash (the files moved; a refusal leaves it). |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/leave` | Signed in | Leave a team project in projects/<name> (a member who reads it): their own rule becomes a "no access" rule of their own, recorded as a leave, so a group that holds them keeps it for the others and they stay out until added back by name. Their private chats in it move to their own chats; audited. 409 project_last_member (nobody else reads it), project_personal, project_not_leavable (not in place or in the trash). Anyone else 404. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/:id` | Signed in | Delete the project. A team project in projects/<name> whose folder is in place goes to the trash with its folder first (it stays, inTrash, until restored); a second DELETE, or any other project: for good (the creator or an admin; private chats stay, without project; its shared chats go to their creators' trash and stop being shared, or are deleted for good when the creator would not see the project). |

## Memories

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/memories` | Signed in | Own memories, newest first, with how many the AI gets now. |
| `POST` | `/api/memories` | Signed in | Add a memory of one's own (same limits as the AI's remember). |
| `PATCH` | `/api/memories/:id` | Signed in | Correct the text of one of the own memories. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/memories/:id` | Signed in | Forget one memory. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/memories` | Signed in | Forget everything. |

## Skills

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/skills/popular` | Signed in | Last 30 days of usage counts for currently readable skills, with no user identities or prompts. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/examples` | Signed in | What the team prepared, read as the caller (Home's first screen): the team and group skills they can use with Trina's example for a kept skill at its own pack path, the team folder's document count (as the caller, all levels down, at most 100, without the brand folder and system files; null when they cannot read it), the invite's skill when they can use it, whether they ran a team skill, and whether a company profile is saved. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills` | Signed in | Skills the caller can use: skills/**/*.md with a name header that the caller can read, the skills of the groups they belong to (groups/<folder>/skills/, with `group`), and their own personal skills (users/<caller>/skills/), by name. One name: personal > group > team > project. `?projectId=` is the list of a chat in that project (its skills with `project`, while the caller sees it). `?shadowed=1` also lists the skills that lost to a better tier, each with `shadowedBy` (the Team skills page); `?groups=1` (owner and admins only) adds the skills of the groups they are not in, each with `group` and `notMember`, to manage them; `?projects=1` adds the skills of every project the caller sees, each with `project` and, when a wider skill of its name runs instead, `shadowedBy`. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/move` | Signed in | Where one of the caller's skills can move: its files, its whole text and each other level with who gains and who loses it (counts only), or why not. |
| `POST` | `/api/skills/move` | Signed in | Move a skill to another level (write on both places, no skill of that name there, a SKILL.md folder for a project). `token` comes from GET /api/skills/move: a changed file or target refuses (409). Audited (`skills.move`, with both levels and the counts) and announced like every skill change. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/issues` | Signed in | Skill entries the caller can read that do not load: an invalid SKILL.md (also a name that is not its folder name) or a legacy file with a broken header. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/overview` | Signed in | The skills folders the caller manages / can suggest into, and how many suggestions wait. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/suggestions` | Signed in | My suggestions, or (scope=review) the suggestions for skills folders I manage. Nobody else sees them. |
| `GET` | `/api/skills/suggestions/:id` | Signed in | One suggestion: its suggester and the managers of its target folder only (404 for anyone else). |
| `POST` | `/api/skills/suggestions` | Signed in | Suggest as skill: from an answer in my chat or a file in my folder; stored on the server (not in skills/); the managers of the target folder are told. |
| `POST` | `/api/skills/suggestions/batch` | Signed in | Members contribute: skill folders from my own computer (read in the browser, keys left there) as one batch of suggestions, each checked again like the skill shares of owners (secrets, scripts, size, names, paths); stored outside the team files until an owner or admin approves; the owners and admins get one Inbox line. |
| `POST` | `/api/skills/suggestions/:id/approve` | Signed in | Register: a manager of the target folder writes it under skills/ (audited, version history); the suggester is told. |
| `POST` | `/api/skills/suggestions/:id/reject` | Signed in | Turn down: a manager of the target folder turns it down; the suggester is told. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/skill-changes` | Admin | Every create / edit / move / delete under skills/ (people and AI), newest first. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/skill-managers` | Admin | Who manages team skills: the write rules for people and groups on skills/ and its folders. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/skill-managers` | Admin | "Manages team skills" on / off for a person or group on skills/ or a subfolder: adds or removes their write rule there (audited, like Admin > folder access). |

| `POST` | `/api/uploads` | Signed in | Attach a file (≤ 50 MB) to an own chat: stored in users/<me>/.attachments/<chatId>/. In a shared project chat the caller sees: saved in the project's chat attachments folder (named in the team's language, made when missing; a taken name gets " (2)") and attached as a team file (source team); 403 shared_upload_read_only without write access there. |
| `GET` | `/api/uploads/:id/thumbnail` | Signed in | Small JPEG/PNG thumbnail of an image attachment (a team file: the image itself, up to 2 MB, while the caller can read it). |
| `POST` | `/api/attachments/team-file` | Signed in | Attach a team-folder file the caller can read to an own chat, as a reference (re-checked on every send and turn). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/attachments/:id` | Signed in | Take an unsent team-file attachment of the caller out of its chat. A file they uploaded from their computer into a shared project chat, never sent and unchanged in its place, goes to the team trash (trashed: true); anything else stays where it is. |
| `GET` | `/api/files/find` | Signed in | Files whose name holds every word of q (in any order and any case), among the files the caller can read (newest first); with folders=1 also such folders the caller can see, first. |
| `GET` | `/api/files/search` | Signed in | Lines that contain q (literal text, any case) in the files the caller can read, office documents through their text cache. Rate limited per person. |
| `POST` | `/api/files/move-suggestions` | Signed in | Where files being moved could go (the Move picker): up to 3 folders the caller can write whose names, files and file-list lines fit the files' names, with a confidence; and up to 3 folders the caller recently moved or saved into. No AI call. Paths the caller cannot read: 404. |
| `POST` | `/api/files/move-suggestions/dismiss` | Signed in | Stop suggesting this folder to the caller for files named like these (per person, kept on the server). |
| `GET` | `/api/files/recent` | Signed in | Recently changed files the caller can read (for the attach picker). |
| `POST` | `/api/upload-sessions` | Signed in | Start a chunked upload (8 MB chunks). Expires 24 h after the last chunk arrived (one hour while no chunk has arrived), at most 7 days after the start. |

| `GET` | `/api/upload-sessions/:id` | Signed in | Which chunks arrived (to resume after a disconnect). |
| `POST` | `/api/upload-sessions/:id/complete` | Signed in | Verify sha256 and move the file into place. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/upload-sessions/:id` | Signed in | Drop an unfinished upload. |

| `GET` | `/api/admin/google-drive` | Admin | Whether Google Drive is set up on this server, by whom, and how many members are connected; never the client. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google-drive/client` | Admin | Set up Google Drive with a Google OAuth web client (stored as a private server file; members then connect their own account). Refused on hosted servers, without a public address, and when the operator set the client. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google-drive/members` | Admin | The old members switch, kept for older apps: admin-only, changes nothing (every member may connect their own once Google Drive is set up). |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares` | Admin | Drives shared with the team: account, folders, who may use them; never a token. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares/authorize` | Admin | Start the Google sign-in for a Drive to share with the team (or a new sign-in for one, shareId). Polled and cancelled like an own flow. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares/flows/:id/complete` | Admin | Confirm the Google account: a new share (no folders and nobody yet), or the new sign-in of a share. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares/:id/folders` | Admin | The share account's top-level folders and shared drives, or folders whose name has q. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares/:id` | Admin | Change a share: its name, folders (checked with Google), the whole Drive, who may use it. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/admin/google-drive/shares/:id` | Admin | Stop sharing: the tokens are deleted at once, then Google revocation is attempted. |

## Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Docs and Google Sheets

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/integrations/google-apps` | Signed in | Own Gmail, Calendar, Docs and Sheets connections and whether each can be connected; never a token. |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations/google-apps/:app/authorize` | Signed in | Start the Google sign-in for one app (gmail, calendar, docs or sheets). |

| `POST` | `/api/integrations/google-apps/:app/flows/:id/complete` | Signed in | Confirm the Google account shown by this sign-in; the app is connected. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/integrations/google-apps/:app/flows/:id` | Signed in | Cancel this own sign-in. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/integrations/google-apps/:app` | Signed in | Ask before each change, or Always allow, for the person's own connection. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/integrations/google-apps/:app` | Signed in | Remove this app's sign-in at once; Google is asked to revoke only when it was the person's last Google sign-in here. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/google-apps` | Admin | Whether each Google app is set up, by whom, the APIs to switch on, the team switch and how many members connected; never the client. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/client` | Admin | Set up one app with the same Google app as Google Drive, or its own Google OAuth web client. Refused on hosted servers, without a public address, when the operator set it, and where it cannot run. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team/authorize` | Admin | Owners and admins: start the Google sign-in of the account shared with the team for one app. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team/flows/:id` | Admin | Poll the shared account sign-in started by this same signed-in session. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team/flows/:id` | Admin | Cancel this shared account sign-in. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team/flows/:id/complete` | Admin | Confirm the Google account shown: it becomes the team's shared account for the app (a new one is used by nobody until its people are saved; a reconnect keeps them). `create`: only when there is none yet (else 409 team_exists: another admin connected one meanwhile). Members' own connections are not touched. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team` | Admin | Who may use the shared account: everyone, groups or people (the same rule as a team connection). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/team` | Admin | Remove the shared account at once; Google is asked to revoke only when no other sign-in here uses the same Google account. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/google/own-app` | Admin | Whether the company's own Google app signs in for Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Docs and Sheets, who set it, whether it can be set here, and how many sign-ins a change would end; never the client. |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google/own-app` | Admin | Use the company's own Google app (the downloaded file listing both return addresses, or its client ID and secret) for all five Google apps. Only where the hosting service is the Google sign-in and the operator set no client; existing Google sign-ins connect again. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/admin/google/own-app` | Admin | Stop using the company's own Google app: the client it wrote is deleted and all five Google apps go back to the hosting service's sign-in (or turn off where there is none). |
| `PUT` | `/api/admin/google-apps/:app/members` | Admin | The old members switch, kept for older apps: admin-only, changes nothing (every member may connect their own once the app is set up). |

## MCP and HTTP connections

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/integrations` | Signed in | My personal connections and the team connections I may use. Never a key or token. |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations` | Signed in | A personal connection (403 when the team turned personal connections off). Checked right away; status says how it went. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/integrations/:id` | Signed in | Change a connection: the owner of a personal one, an admin for a team one. A new address drops the stored key. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/integrations/:id` | Signed in | Delete a connection (OAuth: revocation is tried, the local tokens go first). |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations/local` | Signed in | An app on my own computer (docs/decisions/20261118-local-app-connectors.md): the command's shape only, never a setting's value. Always a personal connection; 403 when the team turned these or personal connections off. Checked right away through this desktop window (x-mycel-window), whose app asks once on the computer before it runs anything. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/integrations/:id/local` | Signed in | Change what an app on my computer runs (its owner only). A new command asks again on the computer before it runs. |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations/:id/refresh` | Signed in | Check the connection now; MCP: save its current tool list. |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations/:id/authorize` | Signed in | Start signing in at the service (OAuth with PKCE) in a browser window: an MCP server, or an API with your own app. From the desktop app, loopbackPort names its return address on this computer for services that take only that. `connected`: an MCP server that offers no sign-in and works without one; it is now a connection with no sign-in, and there is nothing to open. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/integrations/:id/always-allow` | Signed in | Ask again before the AI changes something at a team connection: ends my own Always allow there (never the team's rule). |
| `POST` | `/api/integrations/:id/tools` | Signed in | Turn one tool of an MCP connection on or off for the AI (whoever manages the connection). New tools are on. |
| `GET` | `/api/integrations/flows/:id` | Signed in | Poll a sign-in started by this same session. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/integrations/flows/:id` | Signed in | Cancel a sign-in started by this same session that is still waiting: the service's answer to it is refused afterwards. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/integrations` | Admin | Every team connection, with who may use it. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/integrations` | Admin | A team connection; access says who may use it (default: nobody until set). |
| `GET` | `/api/integration-requests` | Signed in | Requests from admins to connect a service as my own connection, still waiting for me. |
| `GET` | `/api/integration-requests/:id` | Signed in | One request to me, in any state (404 for anyone else, admins included). |
| `POST` | `/api/integration-requests/:id/complete` | Signed in | Connect it as my own connection, with my key, or made for signing in next (MCP OAuth: the request is connected when the sign-in finishes). Only the member it asks. |
| `POST` | `/api/integration-requests/:id/decline` | Signed in | Decline a waiting request to me. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/integration-requests` | Admin | Requests admins sent to members, with their state. Never a key. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/integration-requests` | Admin | Ask a member to connect a service as their own connection (a notice and a link for them; waits 7 days). |
| `GET` | `/api/integration-templates` | Signed in | Templates an admin shared with me, each with my connection made from it (or null). Never a key. |
| `POST` | `/api/integration-templates/:id/connect` | Signed in | Connect a template shared with me as my own connection, with my key, or made for signing in next (MCP OAuth). Again with a key: replaces my key. 404 when it is not shared with me; 409 when it changed since the version I send. |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/integration-templates` | Admin | Every template, with who it is for and how many members connected it. Never a key. |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/integration-templates` | Admin | Register a service once for the team; each member it is for connects it with their own key or sign-in. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/admin/integration-templates/:id` | Admin | Change a template. A new address, sign-in method, header or app deletes every member's connection made from it (and its key); they connect again. The address may not have a query (a key there would reach every member). |
| `GET` | `/api/admin/integration-templates/:id/members` | Admin | Who a template is for, each with whether they connected it and when, or whether their key stopped working. Names and states only: never a key, an address or service data. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/admin/integration-templates/:id` | Admin | Delete a template and every member's connection made from it (OAuth: revocation is tried, the local tokens go first). |
| `POST` | `/api/admin/integration-requests/:id/withdraw` | Admin | Withdraw a waiting request. |

## MCP connector (app connections)

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |

| `GET` | `/api/connectors/remote/requests/:id` | Signed in | Inspect an OAuth request, bound to this user and login session. 404 with params.reason request_expired: the request expired, was decided, or another login session opened it. |
| `POST` | `/api/connectors/remote/requests/:id` | Signed in | Explicitly allow or deny an external app connection. The grant is mcp:read, plus mcp:write when `write` (left out: when the app asked for it), plus mcp:rooms (read my conversations) when `rooms` and mcp:rooms.write (send messages as me) when `rooms` and `roomsWrite` (left out: no), plus mcp:admin when the person is an owner or admin now, plus offline_access always (a refresh token whether the app asked or not). `admin` is ignored (an older page sent it). 404 with params.reason request_expired as for GET. |
| `GET` | `/api/connectors/remote` | Signed in | List only this user’s external connections. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/connectors/remote/:id` | Signed in | Revoke an own external connection and all of its tokens. |

| `POST` | `/api/onboarding/files/rank-own` | Signed in | The AI's picks among files the desktop app found on the caller's computer (Documents, Desktop, Downloads), for the caller's own folder: names, folders, types, sizes and dates only, never content. Anyone in the team but guests; a turn of the caller (their AI, their budget) with no tool at all; answers within 30 s (timeout otherwise), its chat deleted after. |
| `POST` | `/api/onboarding/files/landed` | Admin | A file of the welcome step's upload run landed (owners and admins): records the team files step done in the welcome steps, once, when the file is in a group folder the caller can read. |

Answers at once with a job id; the plan comes from the status call. |

The same plan again: the first result. |

| `GET` | `/api/people/:id/avatar` | Signed in | A person's profile photo (members only; cached for a year when ?v= is the current version); 404 without a photo. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/me/profile` | Signed in | Change own name, title and one-line status (length-limited; audited). Nobody can change another person's profile. |

| `PUT` | `/api/me/status` | Signed in | Set your status message: one emoji, up to 100 characters of text, and when it clears (30 minutes to 2 hours, the end of today or this week in the team's time zone, chosen days, or never); only your own. The team sees it beside your name. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/me/status` | Signed in | Clear your status message (also one that starts later); only your own. |

| `POST` | `/api/me/computer` | Signed in | The desktop app tells how long its computer has had no input and whether the screen is locked (every 30 s): while the computer is in use, your phone gets no push. Kept in memory for a minute; shown to nobody. |

## Team chat rooms

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/rooms` | Signed in | The rooms I am in (my team rooms, everyone, DMs, group chats), most recent activity first, with my unread count, the last message, my notification level, my pin (pinnedAt; the app lists my pinned rooms first) and whether I may add apps there (canManageApps, the same rule as the apps routes); alerts: what else decides whether a message rings (thread replies, quiet hours, the team time zone). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms` | Signed in | Open the DM with a person (the existing one when there is one), or make a group chat with two or more people. Not audited: admins do not learn who talks to whom. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id` | Signed in | One room I am in (404 for anyone else, admins included). |
| `PATCH` | `/api/rooms/:id` | Signed in | Set my notification level for a room (all, mentions, off, or my default), or rename it (group chats: any member, and a private channel, a group chat with a name, cannot be left without one; team and everyone rooms: owner or admin members; never a DM, nor a project's chat room: it follows the project's name). |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages` | Signed in | The timeline of a room I am in from my join on (thread replies only when sent to the room too), newest page first, oldest first within it. With around: the page around that message, and newerCursor for the newer ones. |
| `GET` | `/api/room-messages` | Signed in | Search the messages I can see in the rooms, 1:1 and group chats I am in now (q: every word, in any order and any case, a Korean word without its particle and an English one without its ending; "quoted phrases"; from:person, in:room and mentions:me narrow it, and room= to one room of mine), newest first or the best match first (sort), near matches when nothing matched as typed, with the text around the first word found and the rooms of the hits. |
| `GET` | `/api/room-files` | Signed in | Search the files sent in the rooms, 1:1 and group chats I am in now by name (q: every word, any case; from:, in:, mentions:me and room= as for messages), only those of messages I can see, newest first, with the message each was sent with and the rooms of the hits. |
| `GET` | `/api/room-files/mine` | Signed in | The files I sent in the rooms, 1:1 and group chats I am in now, with a message that is not deleted, largest first, with the room of each and how much space they take together ("Files you sent"). Only my own; deleting one is deleting its message. |
| `GET` | `/api/room-files/recent` | Signed in | The newest files (at most 5) sent in the rooms, 1:1 and group chats I am in now, only those of messages I can see and, for a project room's file kept in the team folder, only while I can open it there; with the room of each (⌘K before anything is typed). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages` | Signed in | Send a message as myself (never another author), or a reply in a thread, with @mentions (or @everyone, written as the everyone room word of each language: mentionsAll; in the everyone room owners and admins only) and files; DMs, group chats, mentions and followed threads notify. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/thread` | Signed in | A thread in a room I am in: its root and the replies I can see (none of it when I cannot see the root). |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/file-access` | Signed in | For a team-file link in a room message I can see that does not open for me: ask (I may ask to view it; by: who answers, only when that is the message's author), asked (my ask waits), open (it opens now; link: its /f/ link when only a share lets me in) or no, the one answer for every other case (a guest, a message I cannot see, a path not linked in that message, nobody to ask): never whether the path exists, whose it is or where. Not in the room: its 404. At most 60 a minute (429). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/file-access` | Signed in | Ask to view a team file linked in a room message I can see (a file access request: its owner, or with none the team owner and admins, answer with Share or Decline in Activity). Only where file-access answers ask (else 404, the same for every reason); one waiting ask per person and file; the file requests' limits (429). open: it opens for me now. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/thread/read` | Signed in | Move my read position in a thread I follow forward to seq; its notices count as read. |
| `PUT` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/reactions` | Signed in | Put a reaction (any one emoji) on a message I can see, or take mine off. A message carries at most 20 different emoji: a new one past that is refused (409, reason reactions_full). Never notifies. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId` | Signed in | Edit my own message. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/message-links/audience` | Signed in | Before sending message links into a room I am in: the links I can see that someone who would read my message cannot (yes/no only, never who or how many), and whether "Show message" may go with each. Anything else is left out, the same for a message that is not there. Rate limited (429). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId/hide-preview` | Signed in | Remove the preview of one message link from my own message, for everyone (its snapshot is deleted). The message is not marked edited. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/rooms/:id/messages/:messageId` | Signed in | Delete my own message (its text and files are removed; "deleted" stays in its place). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/read` | Signed in | Move my read position forward to seq (never back); nobody else is told. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/members` | Signed in | Who is in a room I am in (names only; nobody's read position). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/members` | Signed in | Add people to a group chat I am in (any member; active people only). They see it from now on. Not audited. A project's chat room: 403 project_room (its people are the project's). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/rooms/:id/members/:userId` | Signed in | Take someone out of a group chat I am in: its manager, or an owner or admin in it (never myself: leave instead). Not audited. A project's chat room: 403 project_room. |
| `PUT` | `/api/rooms/:id/hidden` | Signed in | Hide a DM, a team room or the everyone room from my own lists, or show it again (nobody else is told; a group chat is left instead). Hiding unpins it. It comes back by itself when something for me arrives. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/pin` | Signed in | Pin a room I am in to the top of my own conversation list ("Pin to top"; nobody else is told). Pinned already: unchanged. A hidden room: 409 room_hidden (hiding unpins it). At most 50 pins (409 room_pins_full). My other windows hear it (room.updated). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/rooms/:id/pin` | Signed in | Unpin a room ("Unpin"); not pinned: unchanged. My other windows hear it (room.updated). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/leave` | Signed in | Leave a group chat; the last one to leave closes it. Not audited. A project's chat room: 403 project_room (leave the project instead: POST /api/projects/:id/leave). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/files` | Signed in | Upload a file (≤ 50 MB) to send in a room I am in; stored outside the team folder, readable by the room's members once sent. A larger file (up to 1 GB): an upload session with target room (POST /api/upload-sessions). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/team-file` | Signed in | Copy a team-folder file I may read now (not a folder, a link or a quarantined file: 404 like a missing one; ≤ 50 MB) as my upload to send in a room I am in, readable by the room's members once sent; with how many other members cannot open the team file (a count). The same unchanged file again before sending: that copy again; past 200 MB of my unsent copies: 409 team_copies_full. Audited when sent (room.team_file). |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/files/:fileId` | Signed in | A file sent in a room I am in (membership checked on every read); thumb=1 for an image preview, download=1 as an attachment. Inline, a page or script type is sent as text/plain with a sandbox CSP: never a page of the app. A file on the safety check's download-only list is sent only with download=1 (503 quarantined otherwise). |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/files` | Signed in | The files sent in a channel, 1:1 or group chat I am in, only those of messages I can see now, newest first, with who sent each and when (the room's Files list). A project's chat room lists only the files it still keeps itself (room storage, labelled roomOnly: files that stayed when a conversation was made a project) and has no list while it keeps none (its files are the project's): 404, as for a room I am not in. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/saved-files` | Signed in | Files of a room I am in that were saved to the team folder and that I can open there now: the place still holds the same bytes and my access allows reading it. Not for guests. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/save-plan` | Signed in | What the "Save to team folder" sheet shows for files of a room I can see: each file (where it is saved already, whether it looks like a personal document, whether it is the same bytes as an earlier one), one folder I can write to pre-select for the files that look ordinary (matched by name, no AI, only when it fits every one of them; else a recent folder; none when every file looks personal) or, with folder, that folder checked; how many people outside the conversation can see it (a count). Rate limited like the Move picker's suggestions. Not for guests. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/save-to-team` | Signed in | Copy files of a room I can see into a team folder I may write, byte for byte (each ≤ 50 MB, not on the download-only list, never into skills/ or as an instruction file). Never overwrites: the same bytes there already (from this file or any room file with those bytes, an identical file of the same save included) count as saved; a different file of that name stays and the copy goes next to it. Recorded in the file history. Not for guests. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/make-project` | Signed in | What "Make it a project" will do to a group chat I am in: its members (the project's people), the guests who block it, how many files move and stay, the folder name for a name, and the members hash to send back. Anyone not in it (admins included): 404; guests: 403 (never open to them). Not a group chat, archived or already a project room: 409 not_convertible. |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/make-project` | Signed in | Make a group chat I am in (a named private channel or an unnamed group chat) a new team project: its active members become the project's people, the room becomes the project's chat room (renamed to it; each member keeps their start; people added later see messages from now on), and the files every member can see move to the project's Chat attachments in the background. Not in it and admins outside: 404; guests: 403 (never open to them). Not convertible: 409 not_convertible; members changed since the read: 409 members_changed; a guest in another place: 409 guest_one_place (params.guestId); no right to make team projects: 403; safe operations: 409 safe_ops. Audited (project.create via room). |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/room` | Signed in | The chat room of a team project in projects/<name> I read (docs/decisions/20261120-project-is-room.md), made the first time it is opened: a private channel named after the project whose members are the project's people (followed from then on: added, removed, renamed with the project). Anyone who cannot read the project (the owner and admins outside it included): 404 as for a missing project. A personal or older project: 409 project_not_linkable. Its making is audited (project.room). `?listed=1` ("New project with {name}"): the room is listed in every member's Chats before its first message (Room.listed). |
| `POST` | `/api/rooms/:id/save-undo` | Signed in | Undo of the one-click Save to project. Retired in 0.5.22 with the project link (docs/decisions/20261120-project-is-room.md): 410 gone for everyone, naming nothing. |
| `PUT` | `/api/rooms/:id/project` | Signed in | Link a private channel to a team project. Retired in 0.5.22 with the project link (docs/decisions/20261120-project-is-room.md): 410 gone for everyone, naming nothing. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/rooms/:id/project` | Signed in | Unlink a private channel from its project. Retired in 0.5.22 with the project link (docs/decisions/20261120-project-is-room.md): 410 gone for everyone, naming nothing. |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/:id/channel` | Signed in | Make a private channel for a team project. Retired in 0.5.22 with the project link (docs/decisions/20261120-project-is-room.md): 410 gone for everyone, naming nothing. A project's chat room: POST /api/projects/:id/room. |
| `GET` | `/api/rooms/:id/files/:fileId/hwp-preview` | Signed in | One page of a Hangul file (HWP, HWPX) sent in a room I am in, as a PNG from the HWP Preview plugin: the team file preview's renderer, limits and cache. Checked on every request as reading the file inline is: a member, the message visible to me and not deleted (404 otherwise), not on the download-only list (503 quarantined). The plugin off or not usable here: 503 unavailable with params.reason disabled, as for a team file. Pages are 1-based. |

## Bring my skills to the team (share proposals)

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/skill-shares` | Admin | Bring my skills to the team or to one of my groups (owners and admins): the candidates from a picked .claude folder are staged outside the team files, checked (shape, secrets, scripts, plugin, size, personal paths, same name in the target) and judged by one AI turn without tools. Nothing reaches the team before apply. |
| `GET` | `/api/skill-shares` | Signed in | The caller's own share proposals, newest first (a Claude Code proposal shows up here as soon as it arrives); scope=review: the open proposals to the caller's groups that they may apply. |
| `GET` | `/api/skill-shares/:id` | Signed in | One share proposal of the caller's own, or one to a group whose skills folder the caller may write: its candidates with their group and one-line reason, the CLAUDE.md team rule and the tools. |
| `PATCH` | `/api/skill-shares/:id` | Admin | Move one's own open share to the team or to one of one's groups before anything of it went in; the same-name checks run again against that target. The group's members who may write its skills folder are told. |
| `POST` | `/api/skill-shares/:id/apply` | Signed in | Share the ticked skills with the team or the target group as the caller (their own save: folder rules, versions, the skill change log); a skill of the same name is merged through a chat with the confirmation card, the CLAUDE.md lines become a team rule and the tools connection templates (no key; the team only). Idempotent per skill. |
| `POST` | `/api/skill-shares/:id/stop-check` | Signed in | End the AI check of the caller's own share proposal now (Bring my skills stops waiting after 30 seconds): its turn is stopped and the share is ready with nothing recommended (ai failed), so it can be applied and no late answer ticks rows. A share no longer checking is returned as it is. |
| `POST` | `/api/skill-shares/:id/dismiss` | Signed in | Drop a share proposal of the caller's own, or one to a group whose skills folder the caller may write (나중에 하기): its staged files are deleted. |
| `POST` | `/api/skill-shares/merge-chats/:id/start` | Admin | Start the merge in a merge chat of the caller's own that waits for them (`Chat.mergeWaiting`, made at the end of the welcome steps): its one restricted turn is queued now, while they look at it. Once per chat: a second call starts nothing. |

## List folders (my own folders for chats and conversations)

| Method | Path | Who | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/nav-folders` | Signed in | My own list folders, both kinds, each in its order, with how many chats or rooms in it I can open now and (chat folders) its 3 most recently active chats. Nobody else's. |
| `POST` | `/api/nav-folders` | Signed in | A new folder of mine at the end of its list. At most 30 per kind (409 nav_folders_full); a name I already use for that kind (any letter case): 409 nav_folder_name_taken. My other windows hear it (navFolders.changed). |
| `PATCH` | `/api/nav-folders/:id` | Signed in | Rename a folder of mine (404 for anyone else's). My other windows hear it (navFolders.changed). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/nav-folders/:id` | Signed in | Delete a folder of mine (404 for anyone else's). Only the folder goes: its chats and rooms go back to their usual place, nothing else changes. |
| `PUT` | `/api/nav-folders/order` | Signed in | Put my folders of one kind in this order: the ids given first, in that order, then the rest in their order before (ids that are not my folders of that kind are ignored, so two devices never refuse each other). Returns all my folders. |
| `PUT` | `/api/chats/:id/folder` | Signed in | Put a chat of my Trina history (mine, a project chat too, or one shared with me that my history shows) in one of my chat folders (moving it from another), or take it out (null). One my history does not show (a project's shared chat I never wrote in, one I hid from my list): 409 folder_not_in_history. A chat I cannot open, in the trash or the server's own draft: 404. A full folder: 409 nav_folder_full. |
| `PUT` | `/api/rooms/:id/folder` | Signed in | Put a room I am in in one of my conversation folders (moving it from another), or take it out (null). Nobody else is told. A room I am not in or an archived one: 404; a hidden one: 409 room_hidden (show it first). A full folder: 409 nav_folder_full. |
